name: Manipur ethnic conflict (Meitei and Kuki-Zo)
started: 2023 (ethnic violence between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities)
summary: Manipur's ethnic conflict between the valley-dwelling Meitei and the hill Kuki-Zo has cooled from its 2023 peak, and an elected government returned in February 2026 after a period of President's rule. Bombings and protests still flare, as when a bomb killed two children in Bishnupur in April 2026.

sides.name: Indian state
leaders: Yumnam Khemchand Singh (Chief Minister from 4 Feb 2026)

background: Violence between Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities broke out in 2023 and divided the state into ethnic zones patrolled by central forces. New Delhi imposed President's rule, which ended when Yumnam Khemchand Singh was sworn in as chief minister on 4 February 2026. This matters because the conflict sits on the Myanmar border, where cross-border militant links and refugee flows complicate any settlement.
year: President's rule ended with Khemchand Singh's swearing-in on 4 February 2026. On 7 April a bombing in Bishnupur killed two children; protests that followed left two dead and five injured, and further protests on 14 April injured at least 18.
situation: As of late October 2026 Manipur is under an elected government but remains ethnically segregated, with sporadic bombings and protests.
technical: 4 Feb 2026: Yumnam Khemchand Singh sworn in as CM, ending President's rule (Wikipedia).
7 Apr 2026: bombing in Bishnupur killed two children; follow-on protests left two dead and five injured; 14 Apr protests injured 18+ (Wikipedia).
casualties: At least 4 killed in the April 2026 Bishnupur bombing and protests (Wikipedia: 2026 in India); no annual total retrieved.

timeline.event: President's rule ends; Y. Khemchand Singh sworn in as chief minister.
Bombing in Bishnupur kills two children; protests follow.

outlook: Watch whether the new government can reopen movement between valley and hills, and whether bombings or targeted killings restart cycles of reprisal.
